#!/usr/bin/env python3

from typing import Union, NamedTuple

class LookupErr(NamedTuple):
    NotFound: str
    EmptyCollection: bool

def safeReplace(s: str, old: str, new: str) -> Union[str, LookupErr]:
    # Variant 4: use parameter names first and second
    first = s
    second = old
    
    # Handle negative inputs specially (though strings can't be negative)
    # We'll treat empty strings as a special case
    if len(first) == 0:
        return LookupErr(NotFound="", EmptyCollection=True)
    
    if len(second) == 0:
        return LookupErr(NotFound="", EmptyCollection=False)
    
    # Find the first occurrence
    index = first.find(second)
    if index == -1:
        return LookupErr(NotFound=second, EmptyCollection=False)
    
    # Replace the first occurrence
    result = first[:index] + new + first[index + len(second):]
    return result

def test_case(name: str, s: str, old: str, new: str) -> None:
    result = safeReplace(s, old, new)
    if isinstance(result, LookupErr):
        print(f"{name}: Error - NotFound='{result.NotFound}', EmptyCollection={result.EmptyCollection}")
    else:
        print(f"{name}: '{result}'")

def main() -> None:
    # Test case 1: Normal replacement
    test_case("Test 1", "hello world", "world", "universe")
    
    # Test case 2: Old not found
    test_case("Test 2", "hello world", "mars", "universe")
    
    # Test case 3: Empty string (EmptyCollection=True)
    test_case("Test 3", "", "world", "universe")
    
    # Test case 4: Empty old string (EmptyCollection=False)
    test_case("Test 4", "hello world", "", "universe")
    
    # Test case 5: Multiple occurrences (only first replaced)
    test_case("Test 5", "banana", "na", "no")
    
    # Test case 6: Case sensitive
    test_case("Test 6", "Hello World", "world", "Universe")
    
    # Test case 7: Replace at beginning
    test_case("Test 7", "foobar", "foo", "bar")
    
    # Test case 8: Replace at end
    test_case("Test 8", "foobar", "bar", "baz")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
